title: Autonomy Proxylet for Safe Incremental Admin Walkthroughs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: On-call and tier-1 support frequently need to run multi-step, low-risk maintenance actions (schema toggles, kv-store repairs, cache invalidations). Existing runbooks-as-tasks are powerful but either too coarse-grained (big atomics) or require manual sequencing. We want a lightweight 'proxylet' layer that can orchestrate short, incremental admin walkthroughs: small guarded steps with automatic pre/post checkpoints, telemetry assertions, and one-click rollback. The proxylet will expose a templated commandlet runner that composes existing runlets (idempotent steps) into a guided flow and enforces safety gates (canary flag, rate limiter, dry-run validation).
acceptance_criteria: Proxylet service accepts a JSON templated walkthrough with <= 8 steps and returns a dry-run validation report
Each step executes in an isolated transaction boundary with pre/post assertions and emits structured telemetry to the admin dashboard
Walkthroughs can be executed with 'dry-run', 'canary-1%', and 'full' modes and support automatic rollback on assertion failures
CLI + Console integration: engineers can trigger a walkthrough from the admin console and see per-step logs streamed in real time
Security: all proxylet executions are audited in the audit log and respect RBAC/KMS policy rules
design_notes: Architecture: lightweight proxy microservice sits between Console and existing runlet executor. It composes steps by calling internal runlet HTTP/gRPC endpoints and manages transaction boundaries.
Safety model: three modes (DRY_RUN, CANARY, EXECUTE). CANARY applies steps to a sampled tenant subset; sampling is configurable per-walkthrough.
Telemetry: emit structured events: step.start, step.success, step.failure, step.rollback. Include tokenized identifiers for correlation to incident and trace IDs.
Backpressure: impose per-walkthrough concurrency limits and per-step timeouts to avoid runaway maintenance during high load.
Rollback strategy: each step must register a compensating step; if missing, proxylet pauses and hands control back to operator with a recommended compensating action.
Compatibility: reuse runloop, idempotency helpers, and existing operator-auth helpers to minimize new surface area.
Trade-offs: adding proxylet increases control plane calls; mitigate by batching telemetry and caching runlet descriptors.
Upgrade path: feature-flagged rollout behind `autonomy-proxylet` feature flag and opt-in for teams during initial phase.
decisions: Decision: use gRPC to call runlet executor for lower latency and typed contracts (declared 2026-03-03)
Decision: require explicit compensating steps in templates to enable automated rollback (approved 2026-03-04)
Decision: telemetry to be emitted to ops-telemetry ingestion (not standard metrics) for richer per-step traces (approved after PM review)
